{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement (Teleglobe USA Inc.)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the APCN 2 consortium agreement — verified findings 
**Position:** We represent the Customer (Teleglobe USA Inc., an Initial Party).

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Five rules are compliant as drafted, eleven are deviations, two clause types are missing entirely, and one (termination for convenience) needs further review because our verification step did not pass.

The document is a multi-party submarine cable construction, ownership and maintenance consortium agreement rather than a vendor services contract, and that shapes the risk profile. Several rules that normally generate friction are satisfied simply because the restriction does not exist: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no non-solicitation, and no MFN burdening us (the only "no less favorable" and non-discrimination mechanics run against the Terminal Parties, of which we are not one, so they benefit us). Ownership provisions also run in our favour — we own what we pay for, and Paragraph 31 binds every Party to confidentiality with no licence over our data.

The exposure is concentrated in five areas. First, liability is structurally unbalanced: there is no aggregate cap and no exclusion of indirect damages anywhere, so our liability to the other Parties is unlimited in amount. Second, there is no supplier-side IP infringement indemnity at all — the only indemnity architecture is reciprocal cost-sharing in Schedule B proportions. Third, Paragraph 4.9 is a full liability exclusion plus warranty disclaimer with no conformance warranty anywhere to offset it. Fourth, the commitment profile is severe: a 25-year Initial Period, capital contributions in fixed Schedule B shares with no right to reduce, a one-year exit notice after the Initial Period, and forfeiture of amounts already paid on a payment default. Fifth, there is no governing law at all — Subparagraph 27.2 deliberately declines to select any law, and Subparagraph 27.1 makes a Management Committee referral (which may impose arbitration of unspecified method and seat) the sole and exclusive remedy, barring any court.

Seven of these items sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and are listed in section 3. Where curing to the preferred position would require collateral rewrites of the consortium's pro rata sharing mechanics (Schedules B and C), we have targeted the fallback and said so.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Short note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 21.2; Para 32.1–32.6) | No IP infringement indemnity anywhere; only reciprocal Schedule B cost-sharing. Inserting fallback Subpara 32.7 with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace-or-refund and a 3x annual charges super-cap. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 2.5 | No IP, work-product or Customer Data construct exists; asset ownership follows our investment share and an IRU expressly does not convey ownership. No redline. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | KDD T8 (§§ 21.1, 21.2, 4.9, 32.2) | No aggregate cap and no indirect-damages exclusion. Adding fallback Subpara 21.3: mutual 12-month fees cap, carve-outs for § 21.2 indemnity, Para 31 confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; § 21.2 Schedule B share limitation preserved. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 22.1–22.6; Para 12) | Our own carve-outs are fine; counterparties have consent-free routes, consent runs to the Management Committee, and no competitor bar. Adding Subpara 22.7 (our prior consent, not unreasonably withheld; competitor bar; declaratory no change-of-control termination right). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No sourcing restriction; the only "exclusive" reference is the dispute-resolution remedy in Para 27.1. Preferred position met. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 23.1, 23.2) | Capacity reclaimed with no payment or credit and no reimbursement of amounts paid, while we remain liable for unpaid accounts — an uncapped penalty in substance. Conforming the no-credit/no-reimbursement mechanics and barring LDs and penalties. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant; Subparas 12.20, 12.22 and 12.7 are freedom-preserving. Preferred position met. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | KDD T8 (Para 18) | 25-year lock-in; no convenience exit for us. Proposed additive Subpara 18.8 (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund). **Verification failed — see section 4.** |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 9.8, 9.9) | Reciprocal, but any Party may audit our cost books with no frequency limit and no notice. Adding fallback once-per-year cap and 15 days' notice; cost allocation already at or above fallback and left untouched. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 27.1, 27.2) | No governing law selected and courts foreclosed. Replacing 27.2 with New York law and exclusive New York County jurisdiction, and conforming the 27.1 sole-remedy sentence. Delaware, California or London available as fallback. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subparas 11.1, 11.5, 22.3) | Assignment element already satisfied by 22.3(a); the grant does not extend to affiliates. Adding a short subparagraph extending the Terminal Station Right of Use to Affiliates, Subsidiaries and Parent Company on written notice. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 (Subparas 15.2, 17.2; Para 4.1) | The non-discrimination standards bind the Terminal Parties, not us; we are a beneficiary. Our sell-side terms are bilateral under 12.20–12.22. Preferred position met. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | KDD T8 (Paras 7.1, 7.2, 12.2, 18.1–18.3) | Fixed Schedule B cost shares for the 25-year Initial Period with no reduction right and capital forfeiture on exit. Targeting fallback: rolling 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | KDD T8 | No restrictive covenant of any kind; Para 21.1 limits the common enterprise to the express provisions. Preferred position met. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / non-renewal notice | Deviation | KDD T8 (Subpara 18.1) | Indefinite continuation after the Initial Period with a one-year exit notice. Shortening to 60 days; no renewal price-uplift mechanic exists, so that element is not engaged. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | KDD T8 (Para 18; Subpara 32.6; Para 31) | No exit assistance or data return obligation; Para 31 carries only a five-year confidentiality tail. Inserting fallback Subpara 18.8: 90 days' transition assistance and data export within 30 days. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | KDD T8 (Paras 4.6–4.9, 10.1–10.2) | Para 4.9 excludes PG liability for non-performance and disclaims all warranties, with no conformance warranty anywhere. Inserting Para 4.10 (90-day Wet Segment/software, 30-day services, repair/replace/refund) and carving it out of both the liability exclusion and the disclaimer. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | KDD T8 (Para 5.3) | Insurance is permissive only, with no coverage obligation or limits. Inserting a fallback covenant (E&O USD 1M; cyber/privacy USD 2M) on the Terminal Parties and Maintenance Authorities alone. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following seven findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook. We should treat these as the negotiation core.

1. **LD (§ 23.2, KDD T8)** — Uncompensated forfeiture of our capital contribution: capacity reclaimed with no payment or credit, no reimbursement of amounts already paid, and continuing liability for unpaid accounts, triggered as little as three months after a due date under 23.1. Uncapped and unrelated to actual loss.
2. **T4C (Para 18, KDD T8)** — No convenience exit in a 25-year term; unilateral exit only at or after the end of the Initial Period, mid-term termination only by unanimous agreement.
3. **MINCOMMIT (Paras 7.1/7.2, 12.2, 18.1, KDD T8)** — Multi-year take-or-pay in fixed Schedule B shares with no reduction right, no shortfall true-up, and forfeiture of contributed capital on exit.
4. **RENEWAL (Subpara 18.1, KDD T8)** — One-year exit notice for the indefinite continuation period; notice windows longer than 90 days are walk-away.
5. **WARRANTY (Para 4.9, KDD T8)** — Full exclusion of liability for non-performance against specifications plus a blanket disclaimer of all representations and warranties, with no warranty and no remedy anywhere. Fails every fallback element.
6. **GOVLAW (Subparas 27.1/27.2, KDD T8)** — Committee-imposed arbitration of unspecified method and seat, with no governing law and courts expressly foreclosed.
7. **AUDIT (Subpara 9.8, KDD T8)** — Unlimited and unannounced audits of our cost books by any other Party; the only control (F&ASC procedures under 9.9) sits outside the Agreement and sets neither frequency nor notice.

We would add that **LOL-CAP** and **INDEMN**, while not classified as walk-away, are the two critical items whose combined effect is unlimited liability with no IP indemnity protection, and we would not recommend signature without at least the fallback positions on both.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Resolve the T4C finding before it goes out.** The proposed Subpara 18.8 did not pass verification and is marked needs_review. There is also a drafting collision: our TRANSITION redline also numbers its insertion as Subparagraph 18.8, so the two proposals must be renumbered. Separately, 18.4 and 18.7 are keyed to Subparagraph 18.1, so an 18.8 exit sits outside both — for negotiation, extending 18.7 to 18.8 is acceptable, extending the 18.4 no-capital-credit rule is not.
2. **Confirm the negotiation sequence.** We suggest leading with LOL-CAP, INDEMN and WARRANTY (the critical/liability cluster), then the commitment cluster (LD, MINCOMMIT, T4C, RENEWAL), then GOVLAW, then the lower-value items (AUDIT, LICENSE, TRANSITION, INSURANCE, ASSIGN).
3. **Take commercial instructions on the consortium mechanics.** For INDEMN, LOL-CAP and MINCOMMIT we deliberately targeted the fallback rather than the preferred position because curing to preferred would require collateral rewrites of the Schedule B (and, for MINCOMMIT, Schedule C) pro rata sharing model. Please confirm that trade-off.
4. **Confirm the governing-law preference.** Our redline selects New York law and exclusive New York County jurisdiction; Delaware, California or England and Wales are available fallbacks if the consortium resists.
5. **Anticipate reciprocity demands.** On ASSIGN, the other Parties will read our consent right as a unilateral veto and may demand reciprocity; we should decide in advance how much of our own 22.3/22.6 carve-out we are willing to trade.
6. **No action required** on IP, EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE, MFN and NOSOLICIT. These are compliant and, in the case of MFN and the ownership provisions, run in our favour; we will not raise them.

*This memo reflects only the verified findings supplied and the sections cited within them. No other provisions have been assessed.*"}
